questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How plastic was invented in the 1950s
Why recycling alone can solve the plastic problem
How to make plastic from plants
The problems plastic causes, and life without it
questions.why: Beth says they'll be asking: is it time to live without plastic?

questions.q: Why does Beth start with the phrase “Plastic is fantastic!”?
options: To advertise a new plastic product
To show how popular plastic once was
To say that plastic is still the best material
To describe a famous song
questions.why: She says it was used a lot in the 1950s as plastic became part of everyday life.

questions.q: How much of global plastic pollution is thought to come from single-use plastics?
options: About 40%
About 11%
Almost all of it
Less than 5%
questions.why: Neil says single-use plastics are believed to make up 40% of all plastic pollution.

questions.q: Where have tiny plastic microbeads been found?
options: Only in the deep ocean
Only in rivers in the US
Inside the human body, and even in breast milk
In fresh fruit and vegetables from supermarkets
questions.why: Beth says they've been found in the human body and can pass to a child through breast milk.

questions.q: Why does making plastic cause problems at every stage?
options: It uses too much water
It needs rare metals
It is only made in a few countries
It comes from fossil fuels
questions.why: Beth says because plastic comes from fossil fuels, making it creates problems at every stage.

questions.q: What did Dr Sherri Mason's research lead to?
options: The US Congress banning microbeads
A new type of plastic bag
The discovery of plastic-eating microbes
A ban on plastic bottles in schools
questions.why: Her 2017 research into microplastics in rivers led to the US Congress banning microbeads.

questions.q: Why does Dr Mason talk about a paper bag at the side of the road?
options: To show that paper is worse than plastic
To complain about people dropping litter
To contrast it with plastic, which nature can't break down
To suggest that we should all use paper bags instead of plastic
questions.why: Soil organisms turn the paper bag back into soil, but plastic is synthetic and doesn't biodegrade.

questions.q: Besides plastic-eating microbes, what else does Beth say is needed?
options: More recycling centres
Making less plastic, especially packaging
Burning plastic waste
Sending plastic waste to other countries to deal with
questions.why: She says we need to reduce plastic production, especially packaging, rather than simply recycling.
